recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what form the expression takes at x = 0 and what you multiply above and below by.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply by the conjugate
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the 0/0 indeterminate form, then multiply the numerator and the denominator by √(1 + x) + 1. The examiner looks for the conjugate line.
lines: At x = 0, √(1 + x) − 1 = 0 and x = 0, so the expression is of the indeterminate form 0/0.
Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate √(1 + x) + 1.

recall.must_convey: That the form is 0/0 and that the numerator and denominator are multiplied by the conjugate √(1 + x) + 1.
accept: it is zero by zero so multiply by the conjugate root one plus x plus one
rationalise the numerator using the conjugate
multiply above and below by root one plus x plus one
conjugate tho numerator ni multiply cheyyali
the numerator becomes one plus x minus one which is x

steps.why: Substituting x = 0 gives 0/0, which is not a value, so the expression has to be rewritten before the limit can be read. The conjugate turns the numerator into (1 + x) − 1 = x, and that x is what cancels the x below.
common_mistakes: Writing 0/0 as the answer instead of rewriting the expression.
Multiplying only the numerator by the conjugate and leaving the denominator as x.
steps.memory_tip: A square root minus a number over x is a conjugate question every time: multiply above and below by the same bracket with the middle sign changed.

steps.label: Cancel x and substitute
steps.margin_note: Second mark. After the x cancels the form is no longer 0/0, so x = 0 may be substituted. Show the cancelled line before substituting.
lines: This expression is defined at x = 0, so substitute x = 0.

recall.must_convey: That the x cancels, leaving 1/(√(1 + x) + 1), and substituting x = 0 gives 1/2.
accept: the x cancels and one over root one plus x plus one gives one half
substitute zero to get one over one plus one
the answer is one by two
x cancel ayyaka zero substitute cheste one by two

steps.why: Only the cancellation removes the indeterminate form; substitution is valid after it and not before. The value checks numerically: at x = 0.0001 the expression is 0.49999.
common_mistakes: Substituting x = 0 before cancelling and writing 0/0 again.
Dropping the + 1 in the denominator and giving 1 as the answer.
steps.memory_tip: The denominator ends as √1 + 1 = 2, so this standard result is 1/2. Store it: (√(1 + x) − 1)/x → 1/2 as x → 0.

insider_note: Multiply by the conjugate √(1 + x) + 1 so the root disappears from the top. The x then cancels, and 1/2 is worth remembering as a standard result.
